text:
nina.patel: Quick help please  I moved back to India and started working from Mumbai on 2026-10-01. I'm still on US payroll but got a bank transfer from a local vendor with an Indian payslip showing TDS and EPF deductions. I didn't sign up for local payroll. Did I accidentally get put on local payroll? cc @arjun.payroll

arjun.payroll: Thanks for flagging. Short read: India can be tricky. If you're resident and performing duties in India, Indian tax (TDS) and employee provident fund (EPF) / ESI rules could apply. We need to confirm whether this was a PEO/EOR run or vendor misflag. Please upload the paystub and bank reference to the HR portal.

mira.tax: A few clarifying q are you an Indian citizen or OCI? How long do you plan to be in India? Are you being paid by a local client or local entity invoice? India has a residency test (>=182 days) that determines tax liability, and there's a US-India totalization agreement for social security but EPF is different. If you remain on US payroll and we can get a Certificate of Coverage, that may shield you from Indian social security, but TDS may still be applied by local pay agent.

nina.patel: I'm an Indian citizen (OCI), arrived 2026-10-01, plan to stay indefinitely. No local clients, paid from Redwood. I uploaded the MXN-looking stub (sorry wrong reference)  uploaded the Indian payslip and bank tx ref now.

arjun.payroll: I see the records: employee country=IN, payroll_vendor=GlobalPayrollIndia (PEO), employment_type=US-employee. Looks like a stale EOR flag on your employee record triggered an India run this month. Vendor indicates they ran a local payroll and generated a payslip with TDS and EPF (<employee share>).

mira.tax: If vendor generated a payslip and remitted TDS/EPF to authorities, reversal is more complex. Options depend on timing: 1) If remittances haven't been filed/paid, vendor can cancel run and recall net pay. 2) If remitted, Redwood will need to reimburse vendor for employer liabilities and either reclaim employee net or gross-up. For EPF, employer and employee contributions are statutory and typically cannot be reversed after deposit; corrections require formal filings.

leo.legal: Also need to confirm employment change: since you plan to stay indefinitely, do we want to convert you to local India payroll? That has benefits/compliance implications (local employment law, termination rules, statutory benefits). If the move is permanent we should consider onboarding you to Redwood India (local entity) or a formal EOR arrangement, but that requires a conversion process and local employment contract. For now, we must fix the immediate payroll error.

arjun.payroll: Action items for Nina (please paste back when done):
```
- confirm bank tx reference and whether net pay was received
- confirm passport/OCI upload (done?)
- confirm whether you want us to reverse local net pay OR keep and adjust US payroll
- attach any local employment docs you signed (did you sign anything with GlobalPayrollIndia?)
```

nina.patel: I received the net INR deposit into my local bank (confirmed). I uploaded passport + OCI and I did not sign any local contract. I did sign a generic "local onboarding" acknowledgement in the People Portal but that was just confirmation of address. I prefer we reverse the local net pay and keep me on US payroll while we decide on permanent local hiring.

mira.tax: Given you plan to stay indefinitely, tax residence will likely be India and Indian tax will apply. But since the company may have mis-triggered a one-off run, request we attempt reversal first. I'll coordinate with vendor tax counsel to see what's reversible: ask vendor if TDS and EPF were remitted. If EPF remitted, we'll need to handle employer/employee obligations; if not remitted we can cancel.

arjun.payroll: I've opened vendor ticket: case_id=IN-DUP-5512. Vendor initial response: local run executed; TDS challan generated but not yet paid; EPF contributions created but employer deposit not yet remitted. They can attempt recall of net pay and cancel the run within 48 hours. If they cannot cancel, they recommend Redwood reimburse EPF employer portion and reclaim employee net.

leo.legal: Meanwhile I'll draft a short addendum instructing vendor to pause any future local runs for your profile and restrict EOR flags until HR/Legal complete conversion decision. Also pause any client-facing assignments that could imply local hiring.

arjun.payroll: payroll-bot: logged case IN-DUP-5512. Assigned: arjun.payroll. ETA vendor recall attempt: 48h.

nina.patel: Thanks  I prefer reversal. Please note I already paid rent from that INR account and money is needed; if reversal can't happen quickly, how will company handle temporary cash flow?

mira.tax: Good point. If reversal fails and taxes/EPF are remitted, Redwood policy is to make the employee whole (reimburse net or gross-up as needed) while we sort tax documentation. We'll also provide documentation of Indian tax withheld so you can claim credit as appropriate on US returns. We'll also discuss whether to convert to local payroll for future periods which may reduce friction.

arjun.payroll: Vendor update: recall requested; TDS challan is generated but payment not submitted; EPF contribution batch is queued but not remitted. Vendor will cancel run if payment window closes without remittance. We'll update in 24h. If cancellation fails, we'll coordinate repayment and gross-up.

payroll-bot: Reminder: employee to keep screenshots of bank credit and not spend funds until vendor confirms recall. Case IN-DUP-5512 updated.

leo.legal: Also recommending we do a quick PE assessment given indefinite presence in India. Legal will schedule a short meeting with People Ops and AP to scope entity or EOR conversion options.

nina.patel: Uploaded receipts and bank screenshots. Thanks for the fast triage. Appreciate it.
